originality.rationale: Direct alias/parameter/result searches were completed and returned no covering exact token-sliding census. Most relevant primary full texts were compared by logical hypotheses and conclusions, and three highly overlapping same-graph published results were read in full. Published independent-set counts are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The closest theorem on claw-free graphs does not apply because this host has induced claws, and host Hamiltonicity or independence-complex homotopy cannot imply component counts of TS_k. Unindexed tables/unpublished computations remain residual risks, not proofs of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Published or unpublished independent-set reconfiguration tables under a different vocabulary or nonindexed host alias could overlap this exact finite census.
Primary comparisons are limited to the reachable full texts and published indexed search results; they do not prove global novelty.
The proof of the large components and exact distances is exhaustive computational rather than a symbolic structural classification of a family.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is the canonical twenty-vertex bipartite double cover of the Petersen graph. Determining connectivity at every feasible number of mutually nonadjacent sliding tokens is a natural reconfiguration question, not an arbitrary slice: occupancy four is the sharp first disconnected threshold, has exactly ten geometrically characterized frozen stars, and occupancy five has ten explicitly structured subdivided-K4 components. The full exact component and distance spectrum benchmarks the same graph under constrained motion. Static independent-set face counts were already known and are not claimed as new; the dynamic structure is genuinely motivated.
